facts.label: The route
facts.value: NLEX from Balintawak → SCTEX at the junction (follow signs for Tarlac, not Subic) → TPLEX to the Rosario exit → up the mountain by Kennon Road (light vehicles) or Marcos Highway.

steps.tip: Take the Tarlac branch, not Subic
Kennon Road (light vehicles) or Marcos Highway; check the advisory that morning

facts.label: Drive time, Manila → Baguio
facts.value: About 3 hours via NLEX–SCTEX–TPLEX with no traffic (DPWH estimate when TPLEX was completed). Weekends and holidays take longer; add time for the mountain road.
facts.note: Official estimate from 2020, not a measured 2026 time. Replace with Jed's own drive log when he does the route.

facts.label: Toll total, one way
facts.value: Class 1 (cars, SUVs, vans) ₱981 · Class 2 ₱2,337 · Class 3 ₱2,941. Balintawak to Rosario exit, VAT included.
facts.note: TRB's own matrix pages (trb.gov.ph) are behind a bot check and could not be opened. No TRB-approved hike found for Feb–Oct 2026.

facts.label: Toll by segment (Class 1)
facts.value: NLEX + SCTEX, Balintawak → Tarlac (La Paz): ₱670 (Easytrip). TPLEX, La Paz → Rosario: ₱311 (Autosweep). NLEX alone, Balintawak → Sta. Ines: ₱440 since Jan 20, 2026.

alsoSee.name: GMA Regional TV — NLEX toll fees go up Jan 20, 2026

facts.label: RFID on this route
facts.value: You need two balances: Easytrip for NLEX and SCTEX (₱670+), Autosweep for TPLEX (₱311+). A merged "One RFID" account can cover both if you enrolled. Top up before you leave.
facts.note: One RFID (Easytrip + Autosweep in one account) launched Oct 2025 and is optional.

facts.label: Kennon Road
facts.value: Open to light vehicles only (max 5 tons). Camp 2 Acrow Bridge is closed, so traffic uses a one-lane detour. Two one-lane sections at Camp 6 (rockshed approach and falling rocks). DPWH closes it to non-residents in heavy rain (it did on Aug 3–22, 2026).

source.name: Baguio City Guide (relaying DPWH-CAR advisory, Oct 9, 2026 6–7 AM)

alsoSee.name: Daily Tribune — Kennon closed to non-residents (Aug 2026)

facts.note: Changes fast. Check DPWH-Cordillera's Facebook advisory the morning you drive.

facts.label: Marcos Highway
facts.value: Passable. It is not on DPWH-Cordillera's not-passable list as of Oct 9, 2026. Use it if you drive a heavy vehicle. In August a mudflow at Taloy Sur, Tuba cut it to one lane.

source.name: Baguio City Guide (relaying DPWH-CAR advisory, Oct 9, 2026)

alsoSee.name: Daily Tribune — Marcos Highway one lane at Taloy Sur

facts.label: Roads closed around Baguio
facts.value: Not passable as of Oct 9, 2026: PMA Road and PMA Cut-Off Road No. 3 (sinking road), Baguio–Itogon Road at Goldfield (landslide; use Ucab–Midas Road), Benguet–Nueva Vizcaya Road at Beckel, La Trinidad (use Marlboro–Beckel or Labey–Lacamen Road).

source.name: Baguio City Guide (relaying DPWH-CAR advisory, Oct 9, 2026)

facts.note: PMA Road closure affects the PMA (Fort del Pilar) must-see.

facts.label: Baguio number coding
facts.value: 7am–7pm in the coding zone: Mon plates ending 1-2, Tue 3-4, Wed 5-6, Thu 7-8, Fri 9-0. Applies to tourists and holidays. No coding on weekends. The mayor can suspend it by executive order on calamity or bad-weather days.

alsoSee.name: GMA News — coding suspended Sep 3, 2026 (still in force otherwise)
Baguio City Guide — Ordinance No. 1 s. 2003 summary

facts.note: 2026 suspensions found: Apr 8–24 (fuel price surge), Aug 4, Aug 10, Sep 3 (weather). Fine ₱500, and the license is confiscated until paid.

facts.label: Coding zone boundary
facts.value: Coding covers the roads inside a ring of perimeter roads. The perimeter roads themselves are free to use: Naguilian Rd, Abanao St Ext, Yandoc St, Legarda Rd, Marcos Hwy (Legarda to BGH Circle), Kennon Rd (BGH Circle to Military Cut-off), Military Cut-off, South Drive, M. Roxas Rd, Bokawkan Rd. You may drive the perimeter but not park on it 7am–7pm, Mon–Fri, on your coding day.

facts.label: Parking in Baguio
facts.value: Street and park-side parking is a main cause of traffic. The city has studied making weekend tourists park at the Baguio Convention Center and ride a hop-on hop-off bus.
facts.note: Only source is from 2022, and no 2026 parking rules or rates were found. Needs a current official source or Jed's own visit.

facts.label: How busy Baguio gets
facts.value: 1,586,890 tourists visited the Cordillera in 2025. 72.92% chose Baguio as their main stop (DOT-Cordillera).
facts.note: Dropped the 2023 count and the 50k–60k per week figure (from 2022) as outdated.

facts.label: BCPO viewBaguio app
facts.value: Baguio City Police app: live traffic, parking slots at tourist spots, crowd estimates, hotlines.
facts.note: On 2026-10-10 the App Store page returned 'not found' (blank page in a browser). The app may have been pulled or renamed.

facts.label: Baguio weather by month
facts.value: Driest Dec–Apr; very wet Jun–Sep (August averages 905 mm of rain). Coldest nights Dec–Mar: record lows 6–8°C. Bring a jacket any month, and rain gear Jun–Oct.
facts.note: PAGASA shows average monthly temperatures only as graphs, so record highs and lows are used instead.

facts.label: Emergency
facts.value: Dial 911 (national emergency hotline, works in Baguio and along the expressways).

facts.label: NLEX / SCTEX hotline
facts.value: NLEX Corporation hotline 1-35000 for breakdowns, accidents and road hazards. Give your km marker and direction.
